literal.prompt: В брошюре USGS «Topographic Map Symbols» каким цветом обозначен класс гидрографических объектов?

sourceReasons: The brochure gives vegetation green among area features and hydrographic-class lines blue. Brown belongs to topographic contours and black to the listed cultural features; neither is the requested green/blue class. The question explicitly names this brochure, so this is not a universal rule for all maps.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Four standalone nominal captions are permitted by the guide: Синий цвет, Зелёный цвет, Коричневые линии, Чёрные знаки each explicitly identify a color. Each can be read as an independent answer to «каким цветом»; no gender/case completion singles out the key. All are plausible map-color alternatives rather than absurd entities. This asks the familiar school-map association vegetation/green or water/blue; the USGS reference limits the convention, not an obscure publication detail. Easy retained. Topic scope: map symbols, within maps-cartography taxonomy. A future style normalization to four color labels is optional, not a factual or grammatical blocker.

fieldGroups.literal: В брошюре USGS синим обозначены озёра, ручьи и другие гидрографические объекты. Цвет помогает отличать этот класс сведений от растительности и горизонталей, которые в том же описании показаны зелёным и коричневым.
sourceReasons: The first-page area and line paragraphs substantiate the named classes and colors. The green explanation explicitly limits the rule to this brochure; the blue explanation says «в том же описании». Both preserve source scope.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Two clear sentences, under 70 words; explicitly state the answer and a distinction/context. No timeless claim about every map or every individual symbol.

fieldGroups.literal: USGS относит озёра, ручьи и оросительные канавы к гидрографическим объектам; их класс на карте обозначен синим.
sourceReasons: Page 1 names lakes, streams and irrigation ditches as hydrographic features shown blue. Legends pages 3-4 visually show blue river/stream/lake/canal marks. This establishes the examples in the note without claiming every dry-water or engineered symbol is blue.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Names concrete hydrological examples; for blue-water this adds lakes, streams and irrigation ditches beyond the generic hydrographic-class prompt. For green-vegetation it supplies a fact about the blue distractor.

fieldGroups.literal: В этой брошюре растительность перечислена среди площадных объектов и показана зелёным.
sourceReasons: Page 1 lists vegetation as an area-feature example and green. Page 4 shows green woodland, shrubland, orchard and vineyard symbols, with a mixed water/vegetation mangrove symbol. The current note accurately summarizes the introductory convention and does not assert all vegetation symbols are uniformly green.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: The note is a useful independent fact for the green distractor in the blue-water card: area-feature classification and vegetation mapping.

fieldGroups.literal: Горизонтали в брошюре показаны коричневыми линиями; каждая соединяет точки одинаковой высоты.
sourceReasons: S1 page 1 explicitly states brown topographic contours and equal elevation; page 2 visually distinguishes these from blue/black bathymetric contours. The current note is about topographic горизонтали, not every contour on every map.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: Useful fact about the brown-line option: equal-elevation geometry adds meaning beyond naming a color.

sourceReasons: S1 page 1 lists other roads/trails, railroads, boundaries and cultural features as usually black, contrasted with important roads red. Legend pages 2-4 show the listed black symbols and exceptions. «обычно» retains the qualification; «другие дороги» echoes the source distinction and does not say every road is black.
fieldGroups.editorialReason: A concrete list about the black-sign option, within the brochure scope established by the question. No claim about all maps or every human-made feature.
